**R1**
- Frontier-scale retraining tail (SAME): Quantity: GPU-hours per re-training (model scale); the largest granted to a review agent is 96 H100-hours per paper (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28850) and the largest priced training reproduction is GPT-2 1.6B for $672 (https://github.com/karpathy/llm.c/discussions/677); unknown above that is what fraction of submissions have a central claim above roughly 100 H100-hours and whether success would rise with budget once agents cope with higher-compute papers, since today scores fall with compute band.

**R2**
- Rigid-object in-hand dexterity by massively parallel simulated RL (DeXtreme, Dactyl) (SAME): Quantity: simulated robot-years under ADR (parallel environments x wall-clock); the largest reported is ~13,000 simulated years over several months on 64 V100s + 29,440 CPU cores (https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07113), which bought 60%/20% real solves; above that it is unknown whether more years raise real success, because both DeXtreme and Dactyl stop at their budgets and neither reports a saturation curve (https://arxiv.org/html/2210.13702v2).
- Whether generative video models acquire contact physics with scale (Physics-IQ, Genie 3) (ELSEWHERE): Quantity: video-model size and training-video corpus; the largest reported measurement is Physics-IQ across eight models with a best score of 29.5/100 and no scaling curve (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.09038); above today's models it is unknown whether scale closes the ~70-point gap to physical variance, which the authors explicitly leave open.
- VLA model size and pretraining compute on the real-data corpus (GEN-0) (SAME): Quantity: VLA parameter count and pretraining passes over the real corpus; the largest publicly measured size is 7B, with 10B+ trained but unmeasured (https://generalistai.com/blog/gen-0); above 7B it is unknown whether post-transition gains continue and survive the corpus's lack of touch, and the data power law is only extrapolated (a prediction is given at 1 billion action trajectories).
- Video-world-model neural trajectories as training data (DreamGen) (SAME): Quantity: number of generated neural trajectories; the largest reported is 240k with log-linear downstream gains (https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/dreamgen); above that it is unknown whether the slope continues and whether it holds for contact-rich deformable tasks, since the seed data is pick-and-place and action labels come from an IDM trained on real data.

**R3**
- Real-time processing of dense fibre and seafloor sensing (ADJACENT): Quantity: channels times sample rate processed in real time (TB/day); largest reported sustained processing is four years of one Monterey Bay cable offline (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.14844) against a projected tens of TB/day statewide (https://sase.caltech.edu/projects/fiberoptic.html); above that it is unknown whether real-time array processing of thousands of kilometres of seafloor fibre would detect precursory slow slip or foreshock migration that point sensors miss, because no such network has been run.

**R5**
- Physically structured, interpretable contact learning (SAME): The quantity is real trajectories and objects; the largest reported is 570 cube tosses (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2009.11193) and seven objects at about 10 s per session (https://arxiv.org/html/2504.18719); above that nothing is known because the method's point is data efficiency (32 tosses suffice), so the open limit is the model class (rigid, inelastic, fixed friction) rather than sample count, and no deformable version exists.
- Neural video world models as simulators (ADJACENT): Model size and training video hours; largest reported training set is 20M hours (https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/06/nvidia-releases-its-own-brand-of-world-models) and the largest measured physical-understanding score is 29.5/100 (https://arxiv.org/html/2501.09038v3); unknown whether scaling closes the remaining 70 points or a different paradigm is needed.
- Rigid dexterity under automatic domain randomization (ADR) curricula (SAME): Training time times curriculum breadth (ADR sample count); largest reported is the XXL run, about 13,000 simulated years over several months on 64 V100s and 29,440 CPU cores (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1910.07113); unknown whether a 10x longer or wider curriculum lifts full-scramble success above 20% or whether the contact-law residual caps it.
